questions.correct_answer: The behavior of a function as it approaches a certain input value.
questions.explanation: A limit describes the value that a function 'approaches' as the input (or independent variable) approaches some value. It doesn't necessarily mean the function reaches that value at that exact point.
options: The value a function reaches at a specific point.
The behavior of a function as it approaches a certain input value.
The rate of change of a function at a point.
The area under the curve of a function.

questions.correct_answer: The instantaneous rate of change of the function.
questions.explanation: The derivative of a function at a point represents the instantaneous rate at which the function's value is changing with respect to its input variable at that specific point.
options: The instantaneous rate of change of the function.
The total change in the function over an interval.
The area under the curve of the function.
The point where the function crosses the x-axis.
